title: "Security and authority"
description: "What each role may do, and what ForgeCycle does not protect against."
sidebar:
  order: 2
---

ForgeCycle orchestrates coding agents; it is not a security sandbox. The default
candidate permission level is unrestricted because the framework is intended for
autonomous local development. Each CLI retains its own authentication and native
permission semantics.

Authority is ordered as follows:

1. Immutable ForgeCycle protocol
2. Explicit task scope and later human-feedback artifacts
3. Repository guidance
4. Inferred conventions

Deployment, publication, remote mutation, communication, and other external side
effects require an artifact that explicitly names both the action and its target.
The objective alone is not authorization.

Decomposer, Planner, and Reviewer are contractually read-only, but for Planner
and Reviewer this is prompt-enforced for portability. ForgeCycle compares Git
state and HEAD before and after their turns. Unexpected mutation pauses the run
with `read_only_mutation` and is never automatically reverted. Likewise, mutations
between turns are not silently attributed to Builder.

ForgeCycle does not read, validate, persist, or print provider credentials. Child
CLIs inherit their normal process environment. Runtime state is Git-ignored and
created with restrictive permissions. Raw CLI output is discarded unless
`debug: true`; debug output may contain proprietary code, tool output, or secrets
and must be handled accordingly.

Files listed in `worktree.copy_ignored` may hold machine-local secrets (SDK
paths, tokens). ForgeCycle copies them into the task worktree with mode `0600`,
only when they are Git-ignored and untracked. Because they stay ignored, a
Builder commit cannot include them unless the agent force-adds them. The
protocol tells agents not to touch `PROVISIONED_FILES`.

Shell text from task or handoff documents is never evaluated by the orchestrator.
Configured governing-file paths must be relative and cannot traverse outside the
task worktree.
Every role may run commands through its own CLI tools within the task's
authority.
